<div class="question-grid"><article><h3><a href="investigations/smolagents-and-langgraph.html" class="">How much control should an agent have?</a></h3><p>Understand the tradeoff between a model choosing its next action and a workflow whose transitions are explicit.</p></article><article><h3><a href="questions.html#evaluation" class="">How do I know the system improved?</a></h3><p>Separate a convincing answer from a useful result. Look at failures, supporting evidence and the behavior of the whole system.</p></article><article><h3><a href="questions.html#context" class="">What belongs in the model&#x27;s context?</a></h3><p>Connect instructions, memory, retrieval and tool results to the information the model actually needs.</p></article><article><h3><a href="questions.html#deployment" class="">What makes an experiment useful to someone else?</a></h3><p>Follow the path from a working example to a reliable, understandable part of a person&#x27;s work.</p></article></div>

## Find a way into the material

- **Build with OpenAI:** start with the [official quickstart](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/quickstart), then one structured output and one tool.
- **Learn through a project:** [LLM Zoomcamp](https://github.com/DataTalksClub/llm-zoomcamp) connects retrieval, evaluation and deployment.
- **Understand agent context:** the [Hugging Face Context Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/context-course/unit0/introduction) covers skills, MCP, plugins and execution hooks.
- **Understand models:** [Karpathy’s Zero to Hero](https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html) and the [Hugging Face LLM Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/chapter1/1) offer deeper paths.

[Browse courses and lessons](library.html?type=course) or [explore all sources](library.qmd).
